title: Source-cell presentation for the operadic outer-horn problem
statement:
Use the families, fiberwise inert arrows, active arrows and incidence diagrams of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence], small simplicial sets and standard horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and categorical equivalences and cofibrations of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $n\geq1$ and $\pi:\mathcal P\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n$ be a small family with space zero-fibers and with every parameter-edge correspondence constant over $[0]$. Require the inert lifts over $(\alpha,\operatorname{id}_t)$ to be $\pi$-cocartesian in the whole family, not only cocartesian after restriction to a parameter fiber; these are the stationary inert lifts used below. Write $\mathcal A=\mathcal P_0$, $\mathcal P^-=\mathcal P\times_{\Delta^n}\Lambda_0^n$, and $\mathcal P^+=\mathcal P\times_{\Delta^n}\Delta^{\{1,\ldots,n\}}$.

The inclusion $\mathcal P^-\hookrightarrow\mathcal P$ has an exhaustive well-ordered relative cell presentation over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n$ of the following form. There are simplicial subsets starting at $\mathcal P^-$, with union $\mathcal P$, and each successor is obtained by a pushout of an attaching map described below followed by a monomorphism which is a categorical equivalence; at limit stages take unions. An attaching diagram can first be replaced relative to its boundary by a diagram whose comparison to it is a categorical trivial cofibration. The permitted attaching diagrams are:

(a) $X_\sigma\star\partial\Delta^d\hookrightarrow X_\sigma\star\Delta^d$ for a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^d\to\mathcal P^+$ all of whose arrows are active and whose final vertex is a color. Here $X_\sigma=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal P}\mathcal P_{/\sigma}$ is the join slice: its $k$-simplices extend $\sigma$ to $\Delta^k\star\Delta^d$ with first factor in $\mathcal A$. The attaching map evaluates this join diagram in $\mathcal P$.

(b) $X_\sigma\star\partial\Delta^d\hookrightarrow X_\sigma\star\Delta^d$ with final vertex of $\sigma$ over $[0]$.

(c) $\partial\Delta^d\star L_\tau\hookrightarrow\Delta^d\star L_\tau$, where $\tau:\Delta^d\to\mathcal P$ ends over $([r],t)$ with $t>0$. The simplex $\tau$ is taken in the whole family: it may have an initial block of any number of vertices in $\mathcal A$, followed by a nonempty block in $\mathcal P^+$. Its arrows, including those across the parameter change, need not be active. The displayed cell adjoins $\tau$ itself as well as its inert incidence extension; the face $\tau$ need not already be in the previous subset. Here $L_\tau$ is the following simplicial subset of the join undercategory $\mathcal P_{\tau/}$. Its $k$-simplices are maps $\Delta^d\star\Delta^k\to\mathcal P$ equal to $\tau$ on the first factor, with the last factor in the parameter fiber $t$ of $\tau(d)$, every vertex of the last factor over $[0]$ or $[1]$, and every base edge from $\tau(d)$ to that factor, and within that factor, inert. Its operators restrict the last factor. These are all arrows over inert base maps, not just cocartesian arrows. Thus $L_\tau$ retains the noninvertible morphisms between possible inert extensions; it is a quasicategory, not the ordinary category of simplices of that quasicategory. Let $I_r$ have the $r$ edge objects $e_1,\ldots,e_r$, the $r+1$ vertex objects $v_0,\ldots,v_r$, and arrows $e_j\to v_{j-1},v_j$ only, besides identities. Chosen fiberwise cocartesian inert lifts give a distinguished diagram $i:N(I_r)\to L_\tau$. For a simplicial map $g:T\to E$, define the left join-cone simplicial set $E_{/g}$ by $(E_{/g})_a=\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta^a\star T,E)$ with restriction to $T$ equal to $g$; its operators are induced by the simplex factor. For any inner fibration $q:E\to D$ of quasicategories and any diagram $f:L_\tau\to E$, restriction on left join-cone categories is a trivial Kan fibration:
$$E_{/f}\longrightarrow E_{/fi}\times_{D_{/qfi}}D_{/qf}.$$
Here an $a$-simplex of $E_{/f}$ is a map $\Delta^a\star L_\tau\to E$ restricting to $f$ on the last factor. Thus a lift of a simplex of cones on the distinguished incidence diagram extends to the full inert-extension diagram with any already prescribed boundary and base. This is a cone-restriction assertion, not a categorical equivalence $N(I_r)\simeq L_\tau$. For $d=0$ this adjoins the object over $[r]$ and its inert projections after their incidence diagram has been adjoined. For $d>0$ the cone at the final vertex of $\partial\Delta^d$ is already present, even when some earlier vertices of $\tau$ are in $\mathcal A$. In particular, for an edge $a\to b$ from $\mathcal A$ to a tuple, the domain is $\{a,b\}\star L_\tau$ and the codomain is $\Delta^1\star L_\tau$; the edge $a\to b$ is a new face of this codomain. There is no requirement that it factor through a color.

The order has these properties. It is first organized by the dimension of the image of the nonempty positive-parameter tail in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^{\{1,\ldots,n\}}$, with faces and their inert associates ordered so that every attaching boundary is already present. Within a fixed tail stage the type-(c) cells run through the whole simplices $\tau$ above, in increasing dimension, including all their initial $\mathcal A$ blocks; limits are taken before advancing to the next tail stage. A type-(c) cell at a vertex and its chosen inert incidence legs precedes the positive-dimensional type-(c) cells ending at that vertex. For $n=1$, the zero-tail stage first adjoins the source cones at colors by type (a), the zero-output source cones by type (b), and then the type-(c) cells with arbitrary $\mathcal A$ prefix and tail image a tuple vertex. Consequently the entire source cone at every tuple, including its mixed simplices and their composites with inert projections, is present before any type-(a) cell whose first vertex is that tuple and whose base image has positive dimension. Type-(a) cells with a color first vertex use its earlier source cone. For $n>1$, a new type-(a) simplex begins at parameter $1$, so its source cone is in $\mathcal P^-$; positive-dimensional type-(c) cells still include the initial $\mathcal A$ blocks not in that horn. More generally every type-(a) cell of positive dimension has its whole first-vertex source cone and its inert projections already present. Every stationary inert edge into a color occurs among the distinguished inert legs, or is identified with such a leg by an equivalence over the same inert base map. All simplices with an $\mathcal A$ prefix and non-color positive tail are covered by the type-(c) cells and the explicitly stated categorical-equivalence comparisons. The filtration is constructed from the source family alone; its local cone-restriction comparison supplies no functor from $\mathcal P$ into a target and assumes no colimits in a target.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.5 and the source-domain filtration in the proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, printed pp. 332–341, steps (1), (2), (3). For the nonsymmetric generalized version in GH Theorem A.3.4, strongly inert means inert with stationary parameter; the incidence diagram includes both edges and endpoints. This is the domain presentation and its local inert cone-restriction comparison, not the target extension theorem; the restriction on p. 341 is a trivial Kan fibration because the chosen projection diagram is left anodyne in the full inert-extension category. Nonsymmetric formulation following Gepner–Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178v4 Appendix A. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact. Repair: the simplices tau_b in step (3), printed p. 340, are simplices of the whole M, not just of its positive-parameter restriction. Their positive tails cover the open base simplex. This is essential for the mixed source-to-tuple faces. The order is the F(m) filtration (p. 335) with the associate ordering (pp. 338–340), followed by increasing dimension of the full tau_b. Stationary inert lifts are globally pi-cocartesian, as in HA Definition 2.3.2.10(a), printed p. 253, and GH A.3.1(1).

proof.text: Work in $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})\times\Delta^{\{1,\ldots,n\}}$. Call an arrow strongly inert when its ordinal component is inert and its parameter is stationary, and neutral when it is neither strongly inert nor active. For an opposite ordinal arrow represented by $\theta:[l]\to[k]$, put $a=\theta(0)$ and $b=\theta(l)$, and write $h=b-a$. Its unique inert-active factorization is the interval inclusion $[h]\to[k]$, $u\mapsto a+u$, followed in the opposite category by the endpoint-preserving map $[l]\to[h]$, $v\mapsto\theta(v)-a$. Assign the parameter change to the active factor. For $l=0$ the interval has length zero. This proves the normal form, including both endpoint projections; identities give degenerate factors. A positive base simplex is new precisely when its parameter image contains $1,\ldots,n$. Its full-family lifts may have an arbitrary initial block at parameter zero.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof, p.334; explicit nonsymmetric interval factorization replacing the increasing pointed-map factorization.

proof.text: Use the normal form to match base simplices. Read a chain backwards through its terminal strongly-inert block, then its preceding active block. A closed all-active chain (last arity one) is a color seed; a chain ending at arity zero is a zero-output seed. Otherwise either the preceding arrow is neutral, or it is strongly inert followed by a nonempty active block. Pair the former with the chain obtained by inserting its inert-active factorization; deleting the inserted vertex is its matched face. The remaining active-then-inert output chains are grouped with their final inert projections. In the nonsymmetric case retain the entire incidence category: intervals of length one give $e_j$, intervals of length zero give $v_j$, and the two interval endpoint inclusions give $e_j\to v_{j-1},v_j$. Thus output partners include the endpoint triangles as well as the color legs. Zero-output partners are included in the zero-output stage; a projection which is an identity contributes a degenerate partner, not an additional cell. Let $F_m$ be generated by the positive parameter boundary, all positive base simplices of dimension less than $m$, and the longer matched partners of dimension $m$. Allow all initial parameter-zero blocks and pull back to $\mathcal P$. This gives $P(0)=\mathcal P^-$, increasing subsets $P(m)$ and union $\mathcal P$. The refinements in the next steps specify actual attaching diagrams, rather than treating arbitrary skeletal cells as join cells.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof, pp.334-335; base matching with its nonsymmetric incidence refinement. GH Appendix A.3 supplies the edge-and-endpoint incidence category.

proof.text: At a fixed base stage, well-order the nondegenerate lifted color seeds $\sigma:\Delta^d\to\mathcal P^+$ by their actual dimension, not just the dimension of their base image. All proper positive-block faces have smaller base stage or smaller actual dimension. The parameter-zero fiber $\mathcal A$ is full in $\mathcal P$, since a nondecreasing parameter chain with all vertices zero is constant. Apply the initial-block assertion of [lem-coef-quasicategory-simplex-join-attachment] with $V=\mathcal P$, $U=\mathcal A$ and this $\sigma$. Its $X$ is exactly $X_\sigma$. Consequently the natural pushout of $X_\sigma\star\partial\Delta^d\to X_\sigma\star\Delta^d$ maps monomorphically and by a categorical equivalence to the actual generated subset. This is the required type-(a) attachment; it does not use the cocartesian horn comparison. The case $d=0$ is explicitly covered by the cited statement.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.5, pp.332-333; Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof step (1), pp.335-336.

proof.text: Next order the zero-output positive simplices by base stage and actual dimension. Their proper positive faces either occur earlier or are among the previously treated matched faces. Apply [lem-coef-quasicategory-simplex-join-attachment] to $V=\mathcal P$, $U=\mathcal A$ and the zero-output simplex. This gives the pushout of $X_\sigma\star\partial\Delta^d\to X_\sigma\star\Delta^d$ followed by its monomorphic categorical-equivalence comparison, as in (b). Clause (b) does not require every arrow of $\sigma$ to be active, so it includes the endpoint partners. At arity zero there is no color projection to select; the zero-output cell itself supplies that part of the source. This is a source attachment and uses no final object in any target.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof step (2), pp.337-338; zero-output source comparison without the subsequent target filling argument.

proof.text: Order the remaining matched pairs lexicographically by $(u,v,c,w)$ of a longer partner: $u$ counts neutral arrows, $v$ active arrows, $c=0$ for a color-ended partner and $1$ otherwise, and $w$ counts pairs consisting of an earlier active arrow and a later strictly strongly-inert arrow. Refine ties by a well-order; group the entire incidence diagram of an output partner together. Here is the face check. A proper face of a shorter member lowers dimension. A nonmatched face of a longer member is old unless it is another shorter member. For the latter, compose the adjacent arrows at the deleted vertex and refactor in interval normal form: removing a neutral factor lowers $u$; absorbing an active factor with $u$ unchanged lowers $v$; moving an active factor past an inert factor either closes the last arity, lowering $c$, or removes an active-inert inversion, lowering $w$. Deleting the factorization vertex is the exceptional neutral face. Deleting the last output vertex is the exceptional output face. Removing an endpoint loses a positive parameter vertex or falls into the preceding rank cases. Incidence endpoint faces are the corresponding zero-output partners, and the shared endpoint of neighboring intervals is the single object $v_j$, so these faces are not duplicated. This verifies that every other face, including the intersections of output partners, is already present.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof step (3), pp.338-339; explicit associate rank and face checks, retaining nonsymmetric endpoints.

proof.text: For a neutral pair with longer base simplex $s:\Delta^N\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})\times\Delta^n$, let $j$ be its inserted vertex. Put $C=\mathcal P\times_{N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})\times\Delta^n}\Delta^N$. Then $C\to\Delta^N$ is an inner fibration and $0<j<N$. Its preceding edge $j-1\to j$ is the stationary inert factor, so the hypothesis on global $\pi$-cocartesian lifts gives the lifts required by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-inner-horn-comparison]. Hence the pullback of the missing-face horn is a monomorphic categorical equivalence. Include arbitrary parameter-zero prefixes as follows. If $Y$ is their base join slice, prove the comparison after joining with every finite subcomplex $Y'\subseteq Y$ by induction on its nondegenerate simplices. For $Y'=\varnothing$ this is the comparison just proved. Adjoining $\Delta^p$ along its boundary reduces the new comparison to the pulled-back inclusion $(\Delta^p\star\Lambda_j^N)\cup(\partial\Delta^p\star\Delta^N)\to\Delta^p\star\Delta^N$. This is the inner horn of index $p+1+j$; the preceding edge is still the same stationary inert edge, so the cited comparison applies over $\Delta^{p+N+1}$. Pushouts and unions preserve categorical trivial cofibrations by the Joyal weak factorization system. Union over finite $Y'$ handles the whole prefix slice. Thus the neutral pair contributes only an allowed comparison relative to all previous faces.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof step (3), pp.339-340; HA Lemma 2.4.4.6 comparison and the finite-prefix induction.

proof.text: Fix an output simplex $\tau$ of the whole family, including its parameter-zero prefix. Put $B=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})\times\Delta^n$ and map $\Delta^d\star N(I_r)$ to $B$ by the base of $\tau$ on its first factor and by the selected stationary inert extensions on its second factor; the cross arrows are their composites with the arrows of $\pi\tau$. Set $V=\mathcal P\times_B(\Delta^d\star N(I_r))$ and let $U$ be its inverse image of the terminal factor $N(I_r)$. The projection $V\to\Delta^d\star N(I_r)$ is inner, and its base is a quasicategory, so $V$ is a quasicategory. The subset $U$ is full, because the terminal factor is full in this join. The lifted simplex $\bar\tau$ in the initial factor is nondegenerate and disjoint from $U$, even when its image in the base has degeneracies. Moreover $V_{\bar\tau/}\times_V U$ is exactly $L_\tau$: its base simplex records precisely the stationary selected intervals, vertices, and endpoint arrows in the definition of $L_\tau$.  By the opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], $V_{\bar\tau/}\to V$ is a left fibration. Its pullback over the quasicategory $U$ is therefore a quasicategory (fill an inner horn first in $U$, then in this left fibration). This proves the asserted quasicategory property of $L_\tau$. Its inert-extension base category is $I_r$: an inert $[r]\to[1]$ selects one adjacent interval, an inert $[r]\to[0]$ selects one vertex, and an inert map between these selected objects is precisely an endpoint arrow. Consequently there is a projection $\rho:L_\tau\to N(I_r)$ recording the base inert extension. Since $B$ is the nerve of an ordinary category, an extension $\Delta^d\star\Delta^k\to B$ of $\pi\tau$ is determined by its restriction to $\{d\}\star\Delta^k$; hence restriction $B_{\pi\tau/}\to B_{\pi\tau(d)/}$ is an isomorphism, and the inert-extension base simplicial sets of $\tau$ and of the one-vertex simplex $\tau(d)$ are both identified with $N(I_r)$. Write $L_{\tau(d)}$ for the corresponding simplicial subset of $\mathcal P_{\tau(d)/}$.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof step (3), pp.340-341; full-simplex inert-extension categories, with GH Appendix A.3 incidence objects and endpoint arrows.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cofinal-relative-join-slice-restriction] to the full subcategory $\{d\}\subseteq\Delta^d$ (in the role of its $A\subseteq B$), to the inner fibration of quasicategories $\pi:\mathcal P\to B$, where $B=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})\times\Delta^n$ as in Step 7 (in the role of its $p:C\to D$), and to the functor $\tau:\Delta^d\to\mathcal P$ (its $u$). The vertex $\{d\}$ is full in the quasicategory $\Delta^d$, and for each $b\in\Delta^d$ the comma quasicategory of arrows $b\to d$ is a single vertex, hence weakly contractible; $d=0$ is the identity case. So restriction $\mathcal P_{\tau/}\to\mathcal P_{\tau(d)/}\times_{B_{\pi\tau(d)/}}B_{\pi\tau/}$ is a trivial Kan fibration, lifting every boundary including dimension zero. By the isomorphism $B_{\pi\tau/}\cong B_{\pi\tau(d)/}$ of Step 7, pulling back along the vertex $\beta_a:\Delta^d\star\Delta^0\to B$ (the prescribed base extension of $a\in I_r$) gives a trivial Kan fibration $R_a:J_a\to J_a^0$, where $J_a=\mathcal P_{\tau/}\times_{B_{\pi\tau/}}\{\beta_a\}$ and $J_a^0=\mathcal P_{\tau(d)/}\times_{B_{\pi\tau(d)/}}\{\beta_a|_{\{d,*\}}\}$, and pulling back along $N(I_r)$ gives a trivial Kan fibration $R:L_\tau\to L_{\tau(d)}$ over $N(I_r)$. The target $J_a^0$ is a quasicategory with the chosen cocartesian edge as an initial object by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Inner-horn lifting first in $J_a^0$ and then along $R_a$ makes $J_a$ a quasicategory. A trivial Kan fibration lifts against all monomorphisms, so it is a trivial fibration of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] and in particular a categorical equivalence; by [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] (2) and the mapping-space preservation clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $R_a$ induces equivalences of mapping spaces, so every lift of that initial edge is initial in $J_a$. In particular an extension with exactly that last edge exists. Choose one, denoted $i(a)$. For each incidence arrow choose its cocartesian comparison; [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] makes the composite from $\tau(d)$ cocartesian and identifies it with the chosen endpoint extension by an equivalence over its fixed base. The choices form a coherent $i:N(I_r)\to L_\tau$: $I_r$ has no nonidentity composable pair, and each required choice and comparison lies in a contractible initial-object mapping space. This includes $r=0$, where $I_0$ has just $v_0$ and the identity lift supplies its initial extension. One may therefore choose the incidence diagram first for the single vertex $\tau(d)$ and lift it along the trivial Kan fibration $R$; lifting all monomorphisms supplies the whole $N(I_r)$ diagram, with any chosen vertex lifts fixed. This verifies coherence without discarding the prescribed higher faces of $\tau$.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof step (3), p.341 (initial objects B_i of the inert-extension categories) and p.336 ("since the inclusion {B} into sigma_a is ... anodyne, the projection map ... is a trivial Kan fibration"), in the coslice form with the final vertex.

proof.text: For $l\in L_\tau$ with base $b=\rho(l)$, the last-vertex equivalence $R$ of Step 8 reduces mapping spaces to those of the one-vertex inert-extension category. There the cocartesian mapping criterion and fixed-base edge initiality give $\operatorname{Map}_{L_\tau}(i(a),l)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{I_r}(a,b)$: for each allowed base incidence arrow the comparison space is contractible, and for a disallowed arrow it is empty. The base projection induces these equivalences, so they respect precomposition by every incidence arrow. To justify the passage from these spaces to the comma category, put $Q_l=N(I_r)\times_{L_\tau}(L_\tau)_{/l}$. By [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] this is a right fibration over $N(I_r)$ with fibers exactly those mapping spaces. The dual classification and mapping-bifunctor clauses of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] identify its classifying functor with $a\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{L_\tau}(i(a),l)$. Projection by $\rho$ gives a coherent transformation to $a\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{I_r}(a,b)$. Every component is an equivalence by the preceding calculation, so [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes it an equivalence of functors. The same right-fibration classification therefore identifies $Q_l$, up to equivalence, with $N(I_r{}_{/b})$. The latter has terminal object $\operatorname{id}_b$; inserting that terminal object contracts its nerve. At $b=e_j$ there is only the edge object; at $b=v_j$ there is the vertex object and the incident edge objects mapping to it (one at a boundary, none for $r=0$). Thus every incoming comma is weakly contractible, including the nullary case. Since $\rho i=\operatorname{id}$, $i$ is a monomorphism. Apply [lem-coef-coinitial-monomorphism-left-anodyne] to conclude that $i$ is left anodyne. Its image need not be full.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof, p.341, left-anodyne assertion; nonsymmetric comma calculation uses the entire incidence span, not a discrete set of colors.

proof.text: For any inner fibration $q:E\to D$ and any $f:L_\tau\to E$, a boundary-lifting square for the displayed restriction of left join cones is exactly a lifting square for $(\partial\Delta^a\star L_\tau)\cup(\Delta^a\star N(I_r))\hookrightarrow\Delta^a\star L_\tau$ against $q$. The opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones], with the left-anodyne map $i$ in the right factor, makes this inclusion inner anodyne, so the inner-fibration lifting property gives the required filler. This holds also for $a=0$, with empty boundary. Thus restriction is a trivial Kan fibration with the full boundary and base fixed, for arbitrary $q$ and $f$. No relative-limit hypothesis is used. The boundary-lifting conclusion is exactly the definition of trivial Kan fibration in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]: $a=0$ gives vertex surjectivity and $a>0$ gives all remaining boundary lifts.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof, p.341: join restriction along the left-anodyne selected incidence diagram.

proof.text: For an output pair, well-order all nondegenerate whole-family simplices $\tau$ whose positive tail maps surjectively onto its shorter base member, by actual dimension. Generate the next subset by the initial $\tau$ block followed by its full stationary inert-extension block. Its join slice is $L_\tau$, including all arrows over the indicated inert maps, not merely cocartesian arrows. Use the pullback $V$, its full terminal subcategory $U$, and the lifted simplex $\bar\tau$ constructed in Step 7. The terminal-block form of [lem-coef-quasicategory-simplex-join-attachment], with this $V,U,\bar\tau$, identifies the natural model with the pushout of $\partial\Delta^d\star L_\tau\to\Delta^d\star L_\tau$, followed by the monomorphic categorical-equivalence comparison. For the endpoint part use the fixed-base pullbacks over the selected vertices and intervals together: the faces $e_j\to v_{j-1},v_j$ are identified on their common $v_j$ blocks, so the model is the join with the full $L_\tau$, not a disjoint join with the color fibers. Their already prescribed faces are kept in the relative attaching diagram. Gluing the fixed-base comparisons over these intersections is legitimate because each is a categorical trivial cofibration relative to those faces; pushout and transfinite composition preserve their lifting property. The permitted preliminary relative categorical-trivial-cofibration replacement realizes these identifications before the cell. This supplies (c), including the face $\tau$ itself. For $d>0$ its final-vertex cone is a proper $\Delta^0\star L_\tau$ face, so it was attached at smaller actual dimension; for $d=0$ the domain is $L_\tau$ and only its incidence diagram must precede the new object.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.5, pp.332-333, opposite form; Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof step (3), pp.340-341, with the nonsymmetric endpoint intersections retained.

proof.text: The ordering includes every initial $\mathcal A$ block before the base stage advances. Deleting a vertex of that block lowers the actual dimension of the full $\tau$; deleting a positive-tail vertex lowers the base stage or meets an earlier matched face by the rank check. Therefore all mixed source-to-tuple boundary faces occur earlier. When $n=1$, at the vertex-tail stage first take the color seed joins (a), then the zero-output joins (b), then the output cells (c) through every full $\tau$ with that tuple tail, including arbitrarily long initial $\mathcal A$ blocks. The union of this stage contains the whole source cone and all its inert extensions at that tuple. A later positive-dimensional active seed can consequently use its first-vertex source cone. For $n>1$ that cone has parameter image contained in $\{0,1\}$, a proper face in $\Lambda_0^n$, so it is already in $\mathcal P^-$. In every case the vertex output cells precede positive-dimensional output cells ending there. This verifies the boundary and ordering assertions without constructing any map into a target.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof, pp.335-336 and p.340: first-tail stage and the full simplices tau_b, not only simplices in the positive fiber.

proof.text: Every nondegenerate base simplex enters a finite $F_m$ and belongs to a seed, a neutral pair, or an output incidence group. Every nondegenerate lift enters the actual-dimension refinement of that group, including degeneracies in its base image; hence the union is $\mathcal P$. The relative boundary-cell theorem supplies the well-order of these sets and their union at limit stages. Each substantive successor is one of (a), (b), (c), with the comparisons proved above. A neutral-pair comparison may be regarded as a successor with empty attachment (take the empty coproduct of cells). Global cocartesian stationary inert edges into a color are the selected legs or are equivalent to them over the identical base inert map, by initiality and the uniqueness clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. The join-cone restriction has already been proved for arbitrary inner fibrations. Empty source fibers give empty joins; $n=1$, $d=0$, and $r=0,1$ are included in the explicit constructions. This proves every clause of the original source-only presentation.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof, pp.334-341, conclusion of the source-domain filtration only.
